title: Cell Cycle Overview & G0 Phase
summary: An orderly sequence of coordinated events where a cell duplicates its genome, synthesizes cellular components, and partitions into two progeny cells. Quiescent cells enter G0 to remain metabolically active without cycling.
neetAlert: Cells in the quiescent G0 stage remain metabolically active and functional, but suspend proliferation unless prompted by specific physiological triggers.

title: G1 Phase (First Gap)
summary: The growth interval separating mitotic exit from the start of DNA synthesis, marked by intense metabolic activity, transcription, and organelle enlargement prior to replication.
neetAlert: During G1, the cell grows continuously and is metabolically active, but genomic DNA synthesis has not yet initiated.

title: S Phase (Synthesis Phase)
summary: The critical period during interphase where nuclear DNA replicates while centrosomes duplicate within the cytoplasm. DNA quantity doubles from 2C to 4C, while chromosome ploidy remains unchanged at 2n.
neetAlert: DNA content per cell doubles (2C to 4C), but the chromosome number remains unchanged (2n). Centriole duplication in the cytoplasm coincides with nuclear DNA replication.

title: G2 Phase (Second Gap)
summary: The post-synthetic gap phase wherein the cell prepares for mitotic division by synthesizing critical proteins like tubulin, enlarging further, and verifying replication fidelity.
neetAlert: Tubulin and essential spindle proteins are synthesized during G2 as the cell finalizes preparations for mitotic division.

title: Prophase — Condensation & Spindle Setup
summary: The initial mitotic stage featuring chromatin condensation into defined sister chromatids, centrosome migration to opposite cellular poles, and disassembly of the nuclear envelope, nucleolus, and ER.
neetAlert: Centrosomes begin traveling toward opposite poles; nucleolus, Golgi complex, and nuclear envelope dissociate completely by late prophase.

title: Metaphase — Equatorial Alignment
summary: Chromosomes achieve maximum compaction and align along the cell's equatorial plane, with kinetochores on sister chromatids anchored to spindle microtubules radiating from opposite poles.
neetAlert: Metaphase is the optimal stage to analyze chromosome morphology; spindle fibers dock directly onto proteinaceous kinetochore discs on the centromere.

title: Anaphase — Centromere Splitting & Migration
summary: Centromeres cleave simultaneously, freeing sister chromatids to become independent daughter chromosomes pulled toward opposing poles, driven by kinetochore microtubule shortening.
neetAlert: Centromeres split simultaneously; daughter chromosomes travel toward opposite poles with their centromeres oriented toward the lead.

title: Telophase — Decondensation & Nuclear Reassembly
summary: Daughter chromosomes assemble at the respective poles, uncoil into diffuse chromatin, and become enclosed by newly reformed nuclear envelopes alongside reemerging nucleoli and endomembrane systems.
neetAlert: Chromosomes forfeit their discrete structural individuality; the nuclear envelope, nucleolus, and cytoplasmic organelles reassemble.

title: Cytokinesis — Cytoplasmic Partitioning
summary: The terminal physical separation of the cytoplasm into two daughter cells, occurring via centripetal plasma membrane furrowing in animal cells and centrifugal cell plate formation in plant cells.
neetAlert: Animal cytokinesis proceeds centripetally through an inward-constricting furrow, whereas plant cytokinesis advances centrifugally through a growing cell plate.

title: Meiosis I: Pachytene & Crossing Over
summary: A high-stakes meiotic prophase I substage where non-sister chromatids of synapsed homologous chromosomes undergo reciprocal genetic exchange mediated by the enzyme recombinase.
neetAlert: Crossing over transpires between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes and is catalyzed by the recombinase enzyme complex.
